Http.//: Kestrel/Caddy-independent request limits. Media never passes through the API (it goes straight to Cloudflare R2 with a presigned URL), so the body ceiling only has to cover an 8 MB card-template asset plus multipart overhead.

ForwardedHeaders.//: Trust X-Forwarded-For/Proto only from these networks. The compose stack sets KnownNetworks to the Docker frontend subnet so only Caddy can assert them; a directly connected client cannot spoof its IP or scheme.

Database.//: Connection-pool and connection-lifecycle settings for a remote PostgreSQL (Neon). Three independent decisions: (1) MinimumPoolSize 0 so an idle deployment holds no sockets; (2) KeepAliveSeconds 0 — Npgsql's APPLICATION-level keepalive is documented as traffic Npgsql sends on an otherwise idle connection (Npgsql's own default is 0), and a scale-to-zero profile refuses to start with it enabled; (3) MaximumPoolSize must stay inside Neon's per-compute max_connections because the API and the worker each run their own pool (8 + 6 + migrations + maintenance = 18 of the 105 usable connections on a 0.25 CU compute). TcpKeepAlive* is OPERATING-SYSTEM keepalive for NAT/proxy reliability and is a separate, explicit opt-in. None of these influences when Neon suspends — that is the dashboard's / Neon API's job (see infra/NEON.md).
Database.//ConnectionLifetimeSeconds: 0 = pooled sockets live until the server closes them. Set e.g. 1800 to refresh them periodically.
Database.//ConnectionIdleLifetimeSeconds: Longer than Neon's 5-minute suspend window, so a connection is never reused mid-suspend.
Database.//KeepAliveSeconds: Npgsql application-level keepalive. 0 = disabled (Npgsql default). MUST stay 0 when BackgroundProcessing:ScaleToZeroFriendlyMode is on; startup refuses a non-zero value in that profile unless AllowKeepAliveInScaleToZeroMode is set.
Database.//TcpKeepAlive: Operating-system TCP keepalive (separate from KeepAliveSeconds). Off by default; enable for NAT/proxy reliability on a latency-first deployment.
Database.//AllowKeepAliveInScaleToZeroMode: Escape hatch for the startup guard. Only set after measuring that a non-zero KeepAliveSeconds is required.
Database.//DeploymentConnectionBudget: Usable server connections on the current compute: 0.25 CU = 105, 0.5 CU = 218, 1 CU = 443, 2 CU = 894. Raise this (values only) when the Neon compute is raised.

BackgroundProcessing.//: Adaptive polling for every background worker. MaxIdleIntervalSeconds is the worst-case discovery latency and is independent of the database plan; ScaleToZeroFriendlyMode is the database-cost decision. With the mode ON, idle polling is raised to at least ScaleToZeroIdleFloorSeconds (must exceed Neon's 5-minute suspend window) and aligned to one shared tick, so the whole worker container wakes the database once per period. Outbox commits still wake the workers immediately through the Redis wake-up channel, so deep idle does not delay a booking confirmation. Set ScaleToZeroFriendlyMode=false on a paid Neon plan (or raise the floor) for latency-first polling — no code change.

Health.//: Readiness probe bounds. Docker probes /health/live (no dependency calls), so these only apply to the deployment gate and to operator requests. Every probe that reaches the database is also activity that keeps a serverless compute awake.

Workers.//: Time-based sweeps. Their cadence is a business decision; BackgroundProcessing decides jitter, tick alignment and scale-to-zero behaviour.

Redis.//: Short-lived, non-authoritative cache only (tenant scope resolution). Never a queue: durable jobs live in the PostgreSQL outbox. Disabled locally, enabled by the compose stack with a password.

DataProtection.//: Directory for the DataProtection key ring. Empty = the default user-profile path (development). The container sets /keys, backed by a named volume, so card-asset delivery tokens and unsubscribe links survive a restart.

Punched.//: Environment identity. In a deployment APP_ENV_NAME (from the environment file) wins; this value is the local default. local | development | staging | production. See infra/config/environment-schema.md.
Punched.//AllowDeployedDevelopment: Set true only for a deliberate Development-mode container. Otherwise a deployed process refuses to start in ASP.NET Development mode (it would load developer User Secrets).

Secrets.//: Optional file-based secrets: file name = configuration key, content = value. Empty disables it; docker-compose.secrets.yml mounts it at /secrets.

Support.ResponseNote: We typically respond within one business day.

Billing.//: No default webhook secret ships in the committed configuration: the billing webhook verifier fails closed when Billing:WebhookSecret is empty. Set Billing__WebhookSecret per environment (Development uses a local placeholder from appsettings.Development.json).

MediaStorage.//: Provider=r2 in every deployed environment. Credentials and endpoints MUST be injected at runtime (Railway/Neon style env vars): MediaStorage__AccountId, MediaStorage__AccessKeyId, MediaStorage__SecretAccessKey, MediaStorage__PublicBaseUrl, MediaStorage__ServiceUrl. The API refuses to start when any of these is missing or still a placeholder. Provider=local is refused outside Development/Testing. Development overrides this section in appsettings.Development.json.
